parsed.explanation: No law criminalises trans identity or expression, borders are not documented as hostile, and there is real civic presence (elected trans legislator, Pride, local SOGIE ordinances in 9 provinces/32 municipalities, school uniform policy). Against that: no working national remedy — the equality bill has failed for 25 years, the human-rights commission cannot enforce, and service refusals by hotels/venues carry little consequence. The worst documented feature is state-imposed custody exposure: trans women housed by birth sex in male dormitories with mandatory head-shaving and safety dependent on inmate hierarchies, with only one southern annex offering mitigation — a tier-1 exposure with no effective remedy for any detained visitor. Documented killings (two in June 2025, a pattern since 2012) are raw counts without denominators, so the violence axis is weighted as societal hostility with thin recourse, not an established rate. Two municipal cross-dressing bans exist on paper but enforcement is undocumented, so they weigh as an unresolved exposure rather than active targeting. This sits below the 0.45 custody-profile anchor (which showed some effective outside-custody prosecution) and well below the 0.55 service-discrimination anchors (which showed functioning remedies).
